summary_1line: Bhishma recounts a cursed dog’s rise and fall to teach that rulers must appoint ministers and servants strictly according to merit and character.

image_candidates.scene_text: The enraged sage points at the monstrous Sarabha, cursing it to revert as the creature shrinks back into a miserable dog.
A sorrowful dog stands outside the rishi’s forest hermitage after being driven away, its head lowered in shame.
The dog’s successive transformations—leopard, tiger, elephant with streaming temporal ichor, lion, and finally Sarabha—unfold under the sage’s mystical power.
